answer: Because the vertex calculation reruns each epoch, the prism weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the mirror settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 64% independent neighbours on the funding graph. A tight ring of 130 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 11 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
